answer: Prove each identity holds one real network position. A grove of beacons sends timed probes each epoch; the agent must answer within a window matching one spot on the karst map. Each reply carries a jade timestamp signed by its beacon, so timing cannot be faked later. A farmer's thousand fakes behind one machine share one latency fingerprint and collapse to one position, earning once. An honest agent answers one probe set, nearly free; a thousand fakes need a thousand separate endpoints, so the attack costs a thousand live locations, not one script.
